newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX ACCESS energy prices flat amid neutral APIs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX ACCESS energy prices flat amid neutral APIs.

text.p: Neutral data on U.S. petroleum and refined products supplies kept NYMEX ACCESS prices steady on Tuesday, trader said.
"It's a reflection of the numbers," said one trader, referring to a weekly supply survey by the American Petroleum Institute (API).
"I don't see much direction from it," he said.

Crude oil on hand in U.S. refineries jumped 6.4 million barrels last week, prompting a sell-off in early after-hours trade, players said. But the decline was soon stopped at $20.28 a barrel, only six cent below the settle.

"People looked at the breakdown, and saw most of the build was in PADD 5 (West Coast)," the trader said. PADD 5 supply numbers, which accounted for 5.04 million barrels of the build, are dismissed as suspect because much of it resides on ships.
NYMEX May crude added a mere cent, traded $20.29 a barrel several hours into ACCESS. About 1,858 lots traded overall and 1,048 in the front month.
Nationwide drawdowns of 335,000 barrels for gasoline and 2.58 million barrels for distillate came despite an increase in refinery runs, leaving industry observers confused.
NYMEX May heating oil trimmed 0.05 cents from the market close of 53.95, with amid total volume at 251 lots, traders said.
Gasoline was sold at 62.90 cents, a 0.23 rise, but traders said thin volume allowed speculator to inflate the market, trading only one lot at the overnight high of 63.40 cents.
Volume stood at 144 lots overall and 126 in May.
